content:
marta (sec-eng): Heads up — new security policy affecting CI credentials. Starting Apr 15 we will enforce short-lived OIDC tokens for all CI->third-party/service access. Long-lived service tokens will be revoked unless migrated. https://redwood.internal/docs/ci-oidc-migration :warning:

alex (platform): Clarify timeline? grace period? and what happens to vendor integrations that don’t support OIDC? :thinking:

marta (sec-eng): Timeline: Apr 1 — orgs encouraged to test; Apr 15 — enforcement begins (automated revocation). Exemptions possible but limited (see doc). Action items below.

devon (infra): We’ll publish a patched runner image with OIDC helper and an env var: RUNNER_OIDC=true. Image tag: rrunner:2026-04-10. Recommend teams upgrade self-hosted runners before Apr 10.

jen (eng-manager): For orgs with many repos, any way platform can help bulk-enable OIDC?

alex (platform): Yep. We can run an opt-in org script to flip the setting and open PRs. Teams must still validate service scopes.

marta (sec-eng): Required steps for every team: 1) Inventory current service tokens (use audit script). 2) Enable OIDC in repo/org settings or upgrade runners. 3) Replace long-lived tokens with short-lived OIDC flows (exp <= 3600s). 4) Submit PR showing successful run and a short verification log.

marta (sec-eng): Quick audit command (example):
```
# list tokens older than 30 days
python tools/check_token_age.py --older-than 30 --output stale-tokens.csv
```

devon (infra): Also handy CLI to check runner config:
```
# verify runner has OIDC helper enabled
./scripts/runner-check --image rrunner:2026-04-10 --check-oidc
```

marta (sec-eng): Policy notes: CI_ROLE must be scoped to minimal scopes and tokens must include an exp claim <= 3600. Example minimal JWT payload: 
```
{ "aud": "redwood-ci", "exp": 3600 }
```

sre-bot: Automated scan scheduled for 2026-04-16T04:00:00Z to enumerate tokens older than 90 days. Report will be posted to #eng-security/reports and owners will get automated tickets.

jordan (sre): We ran a cursory scan yesterday — flagged 14 long-lived tokens across infra and platform orgs. Will DM owners.

jen (eng-manager): Do we have an exemption process? We use a vendor that only accepts static tokens.

marta (sec-eng): Exemptions allowed but require a compensating-controls plan + written approval from sec leadership. Exemptions auto-expire after 30 days and need renewal.

alex (platform): Platform will provide a terraform module and a repo template to make enabling OIDC trivial. ETA: next Friday.

marta (sec-eng): If you find any token older than 90 days, rotate immediately and notify sec@redwood. Any confirmed leak will trigger immediate revocation and incident response. :lock:

jen (eng-manager): Understood — we’ll start rotations today and book time with platform for the bulk enable.

marta (sec-eng): We’ll also add runtime alerts: tokens issued with exp > 1h will generate alerts and open tickets. Noncompliant services will be rate-limited after Apr 15 until they fix it.

alex (platform): Posting an org-wide heads-up after this thread. If teams want platform assistance, add your repo list to the migration spreadsheet. :email:

marta (sec-eng): Closing thread — follow the doc for the step-by-step checklist and run the audit. Link: https://redwood.internal/docs/ci-oidc-migration. Ping me or @alex for help.
